name: Pharaoh
overview: Pharaoh is a male figure identified as the ruler of Egypt during the time of the prophet Isaiah, as noted in Isaiah 19:11. There is no tribal affiliation or additional personal notes recorded about him. His role is primarily recognized through his political position in the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The individual is referred to by the title 'Pharaoh,' which is a designation for the king of Egypt, as well as explicitly called 'King of Egypt' in Isaiah 36:6. The title 'King of Egypt' straightforwardly denotes his sovereignty over Egypt, while 'Pharaoh' serves as the traditional title for Egyptian monarchs without a specific meaning given here.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Pharaoh beyond what is indicated by his title and role as the ruler of Egypt during Isaiah's time. No personal or familial connections are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Pharaoh's significance lies in his position as the Egyptian monarch during a critical period addressed by the prophet Isaiah. His reign is connected to the geopolitical context of Isaiah's prophecies, highlighting Egypt's role in the unfolding history of God's dealings with nations. While details about his personal life are absent, his mention underscores Egypt's influence and interaction with Israel and surrounding nations in biblical history.
